title: Lisse native coefficient morphisms have finite kernel and cokernel strata
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, put $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic absolute-value topology, and use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For any scheme $X$, let $B_X$ be the sheaf of locally finite continuous $\Omega$-valued functions: its sections on $U$ are continuous functions $|U|\to\Omega$ such that every point has an open neighbourhood on which the values span a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-space. Restrictions are by precomposition. This is the coefficient construction used in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], applied to $X$ itself. Write $\mathcal A_X=\operatorname{Mod}(B_X)$. Call an object lisse if it is pro-etale locally isomorphic to $B_U^{\oplus r_U}$ with $r_U$ a finite nonnegative integer, allowed to vary with the covering member $U$. Let $X$ have Noetherian underlying topological space, meaning every descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes. Let $u:M\to N$ be a morphism of lisse objects of $\mathcal A_X$. There exist finite partitions of $X$ by locally closed constructible subschemes [def-weil-locally-closed-subset, def-weil-constructible-subset] on which, respectively, the restrictions of $\ker u$ and $\operatorname{coker}u$ are lisse. The two partitions may be different. No normality, reducedness, or constant-rank hypothesis on $u$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $K=\ker u$ and $C=\operatorname{coker}u$. The exact module inverse image of [lem-sf-native-adic-pullback-exact-lisse] gives, for every $g:T\to X$, the canonical identifications $g^*K\cong\ker(g^*u)$ and $g^*C\cong\operatorname{coker}(g^*u)$: apply $g^*$ to the exact kernel sequence $0\to K\to M\to N$ and the exact cokernel sequence $M\to N\to C\to0$. The same node supplies lisseness of $g^*M,g^*N$ and the comparison $h^*g^*\cong(g\circ h)^*$. These comparisons always use the native coefficient map, not an identification with another coefficient theory.

source.place: Lines 354-361 and 415-423: exact inverse image and composition comparisons in the induction

proof.text: For each closed subset $Z\subseteq|X|$, let $P(Z)$ assert that there is a finite family of locally closed subschemes of $X$ whose images partition $Z$ and on which the restrictions of both $K$ and $C$ are lisse. Induct over strict inclusion of closed subsets. This is legitimate from the assumed descending-chain condition: a nonempty collection of counterexamples with no minimal member would recursively give an infinite strictly descending chain. The empty closed subset satisfies $P$ by the empty family. Fix nonempty $Z$ and assume $P(Z_0)$ for every proper closed $Z_0\subsetneq Z$.

source.place: Lines 346-352: closed-subset induction and empty base case

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme], choose a closed immersion $i:T\hookrightarrow X$ with image $Z$. A closed immersion is a homeomorphism onto its closed image [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $T$ is nonempty. Every open cover of $T$ is a relative-open cover of $Z$, so [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets], applied to $Z\subseteq|X|$, gives its finite subcover. Hence $T$ is quasi-compact. By [lem-sf-native-adic-pullback-exact-lisse], $i^*M$ and $i^*N$ are lisse. All hypotheses for the generic-open lemma are now available; no Noetherian hypothesis on the local rings of $T$ has been used.

source.place: Lines 353-361: closed support as a quasi-compact nonempty scheme

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-native-adic-generic-lisse-kernel] to $i^*u:i^*M\to i^*N$ on $T$. It gives a nonempty open subscheme $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ on which $\ker(j^*i^*u)$ and $\operatorname{coker}(j^*i^*u)$ are lisse. Apply the exactness and composition comparisons of [lem-sf-native-adic-pullback-exact-lisse] to get $(i\circ j)^*K\cong\ker(j^*i^*u)$ and $(i\circ j)^*C\cong\operatorname{coker}(j^*i^*u)$. Consequently the restrictions of the original $K,C$ to this $U$ are lisse.

source.place: Lines 360-361 and 415-423: generic-open lemma and identification with restrictions of the original kernel and cokernel

proof.text: Write $S=i(|U|)\subseteq Z$. Since $i$ identifies $T$ with $Z$ and $U$ is open [def-weil-open-immersion], choose an open $O\subseteq X$ with $S=Z\cap O$ [def-weil-locally-closed-subset]. The map $U\to O$ is a closed immersion: its homeomorphism onto the closed subset $Z\cap O$ is the restriction of $i$, and its structure-sheaf surjection is the restriction to $O$ of the one for $i$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $U\to X$ factors as a closed immersion into $O$ followed by an open immersion, so is a locally closed subscheme. The remainder $Z_0=Z\setminus S=Z\cap(X\setminus O)$ is closed in $X$ and is strictly smaller than $Z$, since $U$ is nonempty. Every locally closed subset of the Noetherian space $X$ is constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset] (Stacks Tag 005L, label lemma-constructible-Noetherian-space). In particular $S$ is constructible.

source.place: Lines 362-406: proper closed remainder and constructibility of the new stratum; Stacks schemes.tex Definition 01IO and topology.tex Tag 005L

proof.text: The induction hypothesis $P(Z_0)$ supplies finitely many locally closed subschemes of $X$ partitioning $Z_0$, with lisse restrictions of $K$ and $C$. Adjoin the single subscheme $U\to X$ from the preceding steps. Its image $S$ is disjoint from $Z_0$ and $S\cup Z_0=Z$, so this is a finite partition of $Z$ with the required lisse restrictions. Every old stratum is constructible as well, since it is locally closed in the Noetherian space $X$ [def-weil-constructible-subset]. This proves $P(Z)$. Taking $Z=|X|$ gives a single common partition, which may be used for each of the two partitions requested in the statement. The induction has also covered the empty scheme.

theorem IsAdicLisseSheaf.isAdicStratifiedLisseSheaf_kernel_cokernel {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [NoetherianSpace Y] {F G : AdicSheaf l Y} (hF : IsAdicLisseSheaf F) (hG : IsAdicLisseSheaf G)
    (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    IsAdicStratifiedLisseSheaf (kernel φ) ∧ IsAdicStratifiedLisseSheaf (cokernel φ)
lean.note: Exact existing native-coefficient statement at Abelian.lean:429-436. NoetherianSpace is solely topological; IsAdicStratifiedLisseSheaf independently quantifies a finite partition into locally closed constructible subschemes for each object. The coefficients and lisse notions are the declarations already recorded by def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework. No coefficient comparison or added ring-theoretic hypothesis.
